tagline: Two approaches to accessible lung cancer screening: programmable RNA detection of blood microRNAs, and exploratory breath volatile organic compound patterns
tagline_zh: 兩條通往可負擔肺癌篩檢的路徑：對血液 microRNA 的可程式化 RNA 偵測，以及呼氣揮發性有機化合物模式的探索性研究
summary: NIS Almaty-Medeu built MiRVOX, two parallel platforms for accessible lung cancer research: Pulmora, a synthetic biology platform for programmable detection of circulating microRNAs in blood, and OncoNose, an exploratory engineering project on volatile organic compound patterns in exhaled breath. The team states plainly on its landing page that neither platform is a clinically validated diagnostic test. The project is framed by hard numbers - 2.5 million lung cancer diagnoses and 1.8 million deaths worldwide in 2022, 12.4% of new cancers and 18.7% of cancer deaths, and 4,429 estimated new cases in Kazakhstan where it is the second most diagnosed cancer and the most common cancer in men. Their education and inclusivity work is extraordinarily large for a high-school team and is written with unusual methodological honesty, including a published disagreement between two of their own documents' participant counts.
summary_zh: NIS Almaty-Medeu 打造了 MiRVOX，兩個並行的平台，目標是讓肺癌研究更易於觸及：Pulmora 是一個合成生物學平台，用於可程式化地偵測血液中的循環 microRNA；OncoNose 則是一個探索性的工程專案，研究呼出氣體中揮發性有機化合物的模式。團隊在首頁就明白表示，這兩個平台都不是經臨床驗證的診斷檢測。整個專案以硬數據定調：2022 年全球有 250 萬人被診斷為肺癌、180 萬人死亡，佔新增癌症的 12.4% 與癌症死亡的 18.7%；而在哈薩克估計有 4,429 例新病例，肺癌在當地是第二常被診斷的癌症，也是男性最常見的癌症。他們的教育與包容性工作對一支高中團隊而言規模大得驚人，而且在方法學上誠實得不尋常，甚至公開了自家兩份文件之間參與人數不一致的問題。

dry.frameworks: An explicit four-step human practices loop (Ask, Understand, Change, Check back) with the questions for each stakeholder group published before the conversations happened, deliberately 'to keep us honest about what we learned afterwards'. Inclusivity was structured as three questions: what prevents participation, whose input should guide our response, and what can we change so people have a meaningful opportunity to contribute - with a barrier-to-response table published for each strand. A five-stage workshop framework (Introduction, Demonstration, short explanation, Practical work, Presenting the result) with three prepared difficulty levels per activity.
dry.frameworks_zh: 一個明確的四步人類實踐迴圈（Ask、Understand、Change、Check back），而且每一個利害關係人群體的問題都在對話發生之前就先公開，刻意是「為了讓我們對事後聲稱學到什麼這件事保持誠實」。包容性工作則以三個問題架構起來：是什麼阻礙了參與、誰的意見應該指引我們的回應，以及我們能改變什麼，才能讓這些人有真正有意義的參與機會，而每一條工作線都公開了一份障礙對應措施表。另有一個五階段的工作坊架構（引入、示範、簡短講解、實作、成果發表），每項活動都預先準備三種難度層級。
dry.dataviz: Barrier-and-response tables mapping each identified barrier to the specific adaptation it produced; a day-by-day accelerator schedule table with focus, activities and output per day; a feedback table mapping each piece of feedback to the implication it had for programme delivery; partnership tables distinguishing institutions from contributions. The wiki also uses explicitly labelled 'Limitation' callout boxes throughout.
dry.dataviz_zh: 障礙與回應對照表，把每一項被指認出來的障礙對應到它實際促成的具體調整；一份逐日的加速器議程表，列出每天的重點、活動與產出；一份回饋對照表，把每一則回饋對應到它對方案執行的意涵；以及夥伴關係表格，把機構與其貢獻分開呈現。這個 wiki 也全篇使用明確標示為「Limitation」的提示方塊。
dry.datascience: Reach figures are reported with deliberate methodological care: the team distinguishes the 70-school partnership network from the 23 schools visited in person, flags that summer attendance figures may include returning children, and separately records mentor-network size versus completed mentoring outcomes. Most strikingly, they publish a 'Limitation: two different participant counts' box stating that their Inclusivity document reports 120 participants in the biocomputing course while the Education document reports 64, that they have not established which is correct, and that neither figure should be quoted until confirmed. They also state that their evidence shows participation and application but that longer-term changes in understanding would require more consistent follow-up.
dry.datascience_zh: 觸及人數的回報帶著刻意的方法學謹慎：團隊區分 70 校的夥伴網路與實際親自造訪的 23 所學校、標示暑期出席人數可能包含重複參加的兒童，並把業師網路規模與已完成的業師輔導成果分開記錄。最醒目的是，他們公開了一個「Limitation：兩個不同的參與人數」方塊，說明他們的包容性文件記載生物運算課程有 120 位參與者，而教育文件記載的是 64 位，而他們尚未確認哪一個才正確，因此在確認之前這兩個數字都不應被引用。他們也表明自己的證據顯示的是參與與應用，而要證實理解程度在較長期的變化，則需要更一致的後續追蹤。
dry.software: Code Against Cancer, a three-module no-equipment computational biology course: 'Find the Bug in DNA' (compare sequences in Google Sheets, identify differences, then encounter sequence search via BLAST), '3D Molecular Tetris' (explore protein structures in Mol* Viewer and relate molecular shape to interaction) and 'Pipeline of Life' (order the stages of a simplified biological analysis workflow on a collaborative Miro board). Lab Ladder, a 54-page illustrated code-free handbook, walks beginners through six tool 'rungs' with screenshots and worked accessions: NCBI (NM_000207), UniProt (P42212), Benchling (BBa_J23100), BLAST, Geneious Prime and AlphaFold (Q9NZQ7). A Kazakh-language facilitator platform, Tagylym, hosts the methodology.
dry.software_zh: Code Against Cancer，一門不需任何設備、分三個模組的計算生物學課程：「Find the Bug in DNA」（在 Google Sheets 中比對序列、找出差異，再進一步接觸以 BLAST 做序列搜尋）、「3D Molecular Tetris」（在 Mol* Viewer 中探索蛋白質結構，並把分子形狀與交互作用連結起來），以及「Pipeline of Life」（在協作的 Miro 白板上，把一套簡化的生物分析工作流程依序排好）。Lab Ladder 是一本 54 頁的圖解、免寫程式手冊，帶初學者走過六個工具「階」，附截圖與實作用的登錄號：NCBI（NM_000207）、UniProt（P42212）、Benchling（BBa_J23100）、BLAST、Geneious Prime 與 AlphaFold（Q9NZQ7）。另有一個哈薩克語的帶領者平台 Tagylym 存放整套方法。
techniques: cell-free reactions intended for use outside a laboratory
volatile organic compound pattern analysis from exhaled breath
simple optical reader concept for low-cost local manufacture

good.publicEngagement: Three large programmes, each documented barrier-first. First Qadam, run jointly with Panheya Robotics (Panheya supplied LEGO sets and robotics mentors, the iGEM team supplied biological content and volunteers), brings practical STEAM, engineering and biotechnology education to children aged 6-17 facing barriers of location, money, institutional setting, health or unadapted teaching formats. Six school visits in January 2026 reached 226 children; the team then contacted over 100 school directors and built a 70-school collaborating network (the Keleshek network), visiting 23 schools in person near Almaty, Taldykorgan and Taraz between February and May with online sessions and lesson recordings for the rest. Their key finding is quotable: access to equipment did not automatically mean access to meaningful participation, because teachers and children often needed help to start using resources they already had. So they trained teachers alongside students and supplied reusable instructions - and by September teachers and older students in nine partner schools were delivering activities themselves, with five school teams entering a dedicated competition league in June after the team helped create an entry route for Keleshek schools. Daniyar, a research project mentor at Al-Farabi School No. 31, reported running his own activity using the materials from their joint workshop. With Integrity Unite, a volunteer organisation supporting students from unstable financial backgrounds, a first online robotics session for 40 children showed the format was too theory-heavy and depended on kit the children did not own; the team responded by building the no-equipment, mentor-supported Code Against Cancer biocomputing course, run over one week in March after two weeks of recruitment, which produced roughly 34 completed mini-projects with 21 in revision and 26 at the idea stage. With 'House of Mercy: Autism Can Be Overcome', a first April session for 15 children revealed that shared LEGO sets meant nothing stayed with the children; the team then partnered with Sheber Bala to add supervised woodworking so each child made an individual wooden honey spoon plus a drawing on ecological and biological themes to take home, used calm communication and named badges, and allowed flexibility in pace, repetition, breaks and individual assistance across roughly eight summer visits of 10-20 children each. Crucially they write that they adapted to the particular group 'rather than treating a diagnostic label as a complete description of a learner' and explicitly refuse to generalise from one group of autistic children to all. An April workshop for 20 children in residential care combined supported LEGO work with age-banded books on innovation and biotechnology. A paediatric oncology visit for 15 children in Bishkek exposed a continuity barrier - the volunteers and the LEGO left with them - so after consulting KAUST iGEM representatives and a Central Asian iGEM ambassador the team built 12 individual hospital kits containing warm socks, stickers, a book, science colouring activities and crosswords, a change prompted by medical oncologist Baurzhan Ospanovich and summarised as a shift in planning question from 'what can we deliver during a visit?' to 'what opportunities will remain afterwards?'. Delivery was in Russian and Kazakh with visual demonstration alongside verbal instruction, three difficulty levels, two-to-four-hour sessions with flexible pacing, groups capped at five where intensive support was needed and 15 otherwise, with three to five volunteers per group, and multiple contribution routes within a session (assembling, programming, drawing, choosing materials, explaining a result, presenting). Second programme: Girls Go First, which targets the gap between interest in STEM and access to mentorship, networks, resources and leadership roles. A January online workshop with Technovation Girls put six female speakers in front of more than 130 girls across CIS countries; a spring global forum with Yurt Space (a girls-led aerospace engineering community) and Technovation Girls drew participants from more than three countries; a National Forum and StartUp Contest in January-February required every project to be girl-led with girls at least a third of each team, drew about 700 applications from around 386 teams, brought roughly 300 participants from 70 teams to finals in Almaty and Astana, and distributed a KZT 1,000,000 prize pool (backed by Women in Tech, InvestlyHub and StemTrades) as seed funding to seven girl-led teams; an April-June Business Case Championship with Astana Hub and its 11 regional subhubs involved 137 teams and 441 girls across 11 regions of Kazakhstan, each girl-led, with the challenge being to examine existing STEM systems and propose ways to make them more inclusive - and the ideas from that championship fed back into First Qadam's own inclusion policy. An ongoing global mentorship programme with the National Student Research Institute links 65 mentors to more than 45 mentees across over 15 countries, 31 of the mentors being FIRST Robotics and iGEM alumni. The team documents one concrete continuation chain honestly and modestly: Aidana, a Grade 11 participant, met judge Alexander Tyutin (Google Developer Groups) at one of their events, he became mentor for her EcoHub project, and her team went on to win an award at Technovation Girls - with the team noting that the award was Aidana's team's achievement and their own contribution was the opportunity through which the mentoring began. They also publish a limitation box stating that mentor-network size and completed mentoring outcomes are counted separately and that further follow-up is needed. Third: two flagship events. 'Can We Outsmart Cancer?', a free online forum on 8-9 August 2026 on Google Meet with five invited speakers (from UC Berkeley, IIT Patna, Oxford and KAUST) plus two student organisers, three tracks (fundamental research; applications, startups and commercialisation; synthetic biology and student participation through iGEM), a 'Truth or Myth?' Kahoot quiz on cancer misconceptions, and Q&A after each talk; 54 participants on day one and 41 on day two (95 participations) from ten countries - Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, the United States, Romania, Tanzania, Indonesia, India, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and the United Kingdom - with an EdTech partner, 1609+, giving three free subscriptions and a 10% discount to everyone else. The team published both their own organising lessons (cold LinkedIn outreach works when personal and specific; one Instagram post is not enough so registration plus a WhatsApp group plus reminders are needed; attendance dropped on day two so send inter-day reminders; split content into beginner and advanced next time) and the speakers' critical feedback (schedule delays, technical difficulties, a suggestion to prepare backup questions). Then the Bio-Innovator Accelerator, a ten-day hybrid programme from 10-21 August 2026 for 55 participants in teams of three or four - 23 in person at American Corner Almaty and 32 online from Almaty, Astana and regional centres - built because promising laboratory developments in Central Asia rarely reach commercialisation. Week one covered problem validation, customer discovery, TAM/SAM/SOM market sizing, no-code MVP prototyping and unit economics; week two covered biosafety by design, regulatory pathways, intellectual property and freedom-to-operate searching in Google Patents, scientific storytelling, pitch decks and a live Demo Day before an independent jury. Eleven named guest lecturers ran the modules, including founders of ArtSkin, Grader.ai, LUMO/AsarQ and SoundVision, NU iGEM members on Human Practices and dry-lab prototyping, and the KAUST iGEM lead on project design and storytelling with optional 30-minute per-team mentoring. Demo Day projects included FermentAI, a computational platform predicting fermentation outcomes and simulating strains and reactor conditions, and MycoBlock, insulation and building panels grown from Ganoderma lucidum mycelium on local oak sawdust waste as an alternative to imported petroleum insulation. Finally, four open-access magazines published digitally in Kazakh, Russian and English, each deliberately serving one reader intent: Synapse (two issues, 15 and 20 pages - what synthetic biology is, iGEM's history from a 2003 MIT course, Kazakhstan's iGEM history from the first Nazarbayev University team in 2013, a five-step roadmap for joining a lab, questions to ask a lab before joining, six career paths, and national grants such as Zhas Galym and Bolashak); Beyond the Diagnosis (24 pages - cancer causes and types, modern treatments, eight myths versus facts, a patient story and clinician insight, microRNA biomarkers); Lab Ladder (54 pages - the illustrated code-free tool handbook); and iGEM Atlas (20 pages - the Oncology Village, award-winning 2024 projects, commercial transitions such as PvP Biologics to Takeda, startup guides). All four are archived in a public folder and offered explicitly as an adaptable blueprint future Central Asian teams may freely adopt, translate and build on, with Lab Ladder positioned as a new-member onboarding manual.
good.publicEngagement_zh: 三個大型方案，每一個都以「先談障礙」的方式記錄。第一個是 First Qadam，與 Panheya Robotics 合辦（Panheya 提供 LEGO 套件與機器人業師，iGEM 團隊提供生物學內容與志工），把實作型的 STEAM、工程與生物技術教育帶給 6 至 17 歲、面臨地理位置、金錢、機構環境、健康或未經調整的教學形式等障礙的兒童。2026 年 1 月的六場校園參訪觸及 226 位兒童；團隊接著聯繫了 100 多位校長，建立起一個 70 校的合作網路（Keleshek 網路），並在 2 月至 5 月間親自造訪了 Almaty、Taldykorgan 與 Taraz 附近的 23 所學校，其餘則以線上課程與課程錄影支援。他們的關鍵發現值得一再引用：擁有設備並不自動等於擁有有意義的參與機會，因為老師與孩子往往需要有人協助，才能開始使用他們手上早就有的資源。於是他們把老師與學生一起訓練，並提供可重複使用的說明文件；到了九月，九所夥伴學校的老師與較年長的學生已經能自行帶領這些活動，而在團隊協助為 Keleshek 學校建立參賽途徑之後，六月有五支校隊進入了一個專門的競賽聯盟。Al-Farabi School No. 31 的研究專案業師 Daniyar 回報，他已用他們共同辦理的工作坊素材，自行辦了一場活動。與支持經濟狀況不穩定學生的志工組織 Integrity Unite 合作時，第一場面向 40 位兒童的線上機器人課程顯示這個形式偏重理論，而且依賴孩子並不擁有的套件；團隊因此建立了不需設備、由業師陪伴的 Code Against Cancer 生物運算課程，在兩週招募後於三月進行一週，產出約 34 個已完成的小型專案，另有 21 個在修改中、26 個停在構想階段。與「House of Mercy: Autism Can Be Overcome」合作時，四月的第一場面向 15 位兒童的活動揭露出共用 LEGO 套件意味著孩子手上什麼都留不下；團隊於是與 Sheber Bala 合作，加入在督導下進行的木工，讓每個孩子都做出一支屬於自己的木製蜂蜜匙，再加上一幅生態與生物主題的畫作可以帶回家；他們採用平緩的溝通方式與寫上名字的名牌，並在大約八次每場 10 至 20 人的暑期探訪中，允許步調、重複、休息與個別協助上的彈性。關鍵在於他們寫下自己是針對這一個特定群體做調整，「而不是把一個診斷標籤當成對一位學習者的完整描述」，並明確拒絕由一群自閉症兒童推論到所有自閉症兒童。四月另有一場面向 20 位安置機構兒童的工作坊，把有人陪伴的 LEGO 操作與依年齡分級的創新與生物技術書籍結合起來。在 Bishkek 面向 15 位兒童的小兒腫瘤科探訪則暴露出一個延續性障礙，也就是志工與 LEGO 都隨著他們離開了；因此在諮詢 KAUST iGEM 的代表與一位中亞 iGEM 大使之後，團隊製作了 12 份個人用的醫院套件，內含保暖襪、貼紙、一本書、科學著色活動與填字遊戲，而這項改變是由腫瘤內科醫師 Baurzhan Ospanovich 所促成，並被總結為規劃問題的轉換，從「我們在一次探訪中能交付什麼？」變成「探訪結束之後還會留下哪些機會？」。活動以俄語與哈薩克語進行，口頭說明之外並搭配視覺示範，提供三種難度層級，每場兩到四小時且步調彈性，需要密集協助時每組上限五人、其餘情況上限 15 人，每組配三到五位志工，並在同一場活動中提供多種參與途徑（組裝、寫程式、繪圖、挑選材料、解說結果、上台發表）。第二個方案是 Girls Go First，針對的是「對 STEM 有興趣」與「能取得業師、人脈、資源與領導職位」之間的落差。一月與 Technovation Girls 合辦的線上工作坊，讓六位女性講者面向 CIS 各國超過 130 位女孩；春季與 Yurt Space（一個由女孩主導的航太工程社群）及 Technovation Girls 合辦的全球論壇，吸引了來自三個以上國家的參與者；一月至二月的全國論壇與新創競賽要求每個專案都必須由女生主導、且每隊至少三分之一為女生，共收到約 386 支隊伍的約 700 份申請，最後約 300 位來自 70 支隊伍的參與者進入 Almaty 與 Astana 的決賽，並把 100 萬 KZT 的獎金池（由 Women in Tech、InvestlyHub 與 StemTrades 支持）作為種子資金分配給七支由女生主導的隊伍；四月至六月與 Astana Hub 及其 11 個區域分部合辦的商業案例錦標賽，則有來自哈薩克 11 個地區的 137 支隊伍、441 位女生參與，每隊都由女生主導，題目是檢視現有的 STEM 體系並提出讓它更具包容性的方法，而這場錦標賽產出的想法又回饋到 First Qadam 自己的包容政策之中。一個與 National Student Research Institute 合辦、持續進行中的全球業師方案，把 65 位業師與超過 15 個國家、45 位以上的受輔導者連結起來，其中 31 位業師是 FIRST Robotics 與 iGEM 的校友。團隊誠實且不誇大地記錄了一條具體的延續鏈：11 年級參與者 Aidana 在他們某場活動中認識了評審 Alexander Tyutin（Google Developer Groups），他後來成為她 EcoHub 專案的業師，而她的隊伍最終在 Technovation Girls 獲獎；團隊並註明該獎項是 Aidana 隊伍的成就，他們自己的貢獻只是提供了那個讓輔導關係得以開始的機會。他們也公開了一個限制方塊，說明業師網路規模與已完成的輔導成果是分開計算的，而且需要進一步追蹤。第三個部分是兩場旗艦活動。「Can We Outsmart Cancer?」是 2026 年 8 月 8 至 9 日在 Google Meet 上舉行的免費線上論壇，有五位受邀講者（來自 UC Berkeley、IIT Patna、Oxford 與 KAUST）加上兩位學生籌辦者、三條分軌（基礎研究；應用、新創與商業化；合成生物學與透過 iGEM 參與），一場針對癌症迷思的「Truth or Myth?」Kahoot 問答，以及每場演講後的問答；第一天有 54 人、第二天有 41 人參與（合計 95 人次），來自十個國家，即哈薩克、吉爾吉斯、美國、羅馬尼亞、坦尚尼亞、印尼、印度、巴基斯坦、沙烏地阿拉伯與英國，並有一個 EdTech 夥伴 1609+ 提供三份免費訂閱以及給其餘所有人的 10% 折扣。團隊同時公開了自己的籌辦心得（冷接觸式的 LinkedIn 邀約在夠個人化且夠具體時是有效的；只發一則 Instagram 貼文不夠，必須有報名加 WhatsApp 群組再加提醒；第二天出席率下降，所以要在兩日之間發提醒；下次要把內容拆成初階與進階），以及講者們的批評性回饋（議程延遲、技術問題，以及建議事先準備備用問題）。接著是 Bio-Innovator Accelerator，2026 年 8 月 10 至 21 日為期十天的混合形式方案，55 位參與者分成三到四人一組，其中 23 人在 American Corner Almaty 實體參與，32 人從 Almaty、Astana 與各區域中心線上參與；開辦這個方案的原因是中亞有前景的實驗室成果很少走到商業化。第一週涵蓋問題驗證、客戶探索、TAM/SAM/SOM 市場規模估算、免寫程式的 MVP 原型製作與單位經濟；第二週涵蓋設計階段即納入生物安全、法規路徑、智慧財產與在 Google Patents 做自由實施檢索、科學敘事、提案簡報，以及在獨立評審團面前的現場 Demo Day。十一位具名的客座講師負責各模組，包括 ArtSkin、Grader.ai、LUMO/AsarQ 與 SoundVision 的創辦人、負責人類實踐與乾實驗原型的 NU iGEM 成員，以及負責專案設計與敘事的 KAUST iGEM 負責人，後者並提供每隊 30 分鐘的選擇性輔導。Demo Day 的專案包括 FermentAI，一個預測發酵結果並模擬菌株與反應器條件的運算平台；以及 MycoBlock，以 Ganoderma lucidum 菌絲體在當地橡木木屑廢料上長成的隔熱與建築板材，用以替代進口的石油基隔熱材。最後是四份開放取用的刊物，以哈薩克語、俄語與英語數位發行，每一份都刻意服務一種讀者意圖：Synapse（兩期，15 頁與 20 頁，介紹合成生物學是什麼、iGEM 自 2003 年 MIT 一門課起的歷史、哈薩克自 2013 年第一支 Nazarbayev University 隊伍以來的 iGEM 歷史、加入實驗室的五步路線圖、加入之前該問實驗室哪些問題、六條職涯路徑，以及 Zhas Galym 與 Bolashak 等國家級補助）；Beyond the Diagnosis（24 頁，癌症成因與類型、現代治療方式、八組迷思與事實對照、一則病患故事與臨床醫師見解、microRNA 生物標記）；Lab Ladder（54 頁的圖解免寫程式工具手冊）；以及 iGEM Atlas（20 頁，介紹 Oncology Village、2024 年的獲獎專案、PvP Biologics 併入 Takeda 這類商業化轉型，以及新創指南）。四份刊物全部存放在一個公開資料夾中，並明確作為一份可調整套用的藍圖，供未來的中亞團隊自由採用、翻譯與延伸，其中 Lab Ladder 被定位為新成員的上手手冊。
good.ihp: The human practices page is built around a published commitment: list the groups whose answers would change the project and publish the questions for each before the conversations, so the team cannot retrofit what it learned. Five stakeholder groups are specified with their questions - clinicians (where in the pathway a triage test could help, what accuracy would earn their trust, what a false alarm costs), patients and the public (whether breathing into a device is acceptable and where, how an elevated-risk result should be explained, what should happen next and how fast), public health and policy (how lung cancer screening is organised in Kazakhstan today, what evidence a pilot would require, which regions have least CT access), bioethics and biosafety (what is required before collecting human breath samples, how to handle results the project is not qualified to interpret, what biosafety rules apply to cell-free reactions used outside a lab) and engineers and manufacturers (what a simple optical reader would cost to build locally, how cell-free reagents could ship without a cold chain). The team's framing sentence is that a screening test is a health-system decision, not a device decision, and that affordability, portability and follow-up capacity shape the design as much as the biology.
good.ihp_zh: 人類實踐頁面是圍繞一項公開承諾建起來的：先列出哪些群體的回答會改變這個專案，並在對話之前就公開對每一群體要問的問題，使團隊無法事後把學到的東西回頭套上去。文中具體指定了五個利害關係人群體及其問題，包括臨床醫師（在整個診療路徑的哪一段，一個分流檢測會有幫助；什麼樣的準確度才能贏得他們的信任；一次假警報的代價是什麼）、病患與一般公眾（對著一個裝置吹氣是否可接受、在什麼場所可接受；風險升高的結果該如何解釋；接下來該怎麼辦、要多快）、公共衛生與政策（哈薩克目前的肺癌篩檢如何組織；一項試辦計畫需要什麼樣的證據；哪些地區最缺 CT）、生物倫理與生物安全（採集人體呼氣樣本之前必須具備什麼；對於本專案沒有資格解讀的結果該如何處理；在實驗室外使用無細胞反應時適用哪些生物安全規範），以及工程師與製造商（一台簡易光學讀取器在本地自製要多少成本；無細胞試劑如何在沒有冷鏈的情況下運送）。團隊用來定調的那句話是：篩檢檢測是一個衛生體系的決定，而不是一個裝置的決定；而可負擔性、可攜性與後續追蹤能力對設計的影響，與生物學本身一樣大。
good.realWorld: Consent and privacy practice is unusually explicit for a high-school team: activities were pre-coordinated with receiving organisations through correspondence, calls and preliminary visits; parents or legal representatives gave permission, with photography consented separately so children whose parents declined were not photographed; participants could decline an activity, a photograph or a question; access to original photographs and video was restricted to designated representatives of the visiting team and the receiving organisation and publication followed agreement with the organisation; and the team states that their photographs therefore do not represent every participant or activity. Prize-pool money in Girls Go First went through official consent-related documentation. Open resources: four trilingual magazines in a public folder, lesson recordings, age-banded books, science colouring activities and crosswords, guides and workshop methodology, with the full methodology available through partnership at a published contact address. External recognition includes a letter dated 22 April 2026 from the Ministry of Health of the Kyrgyz Republic thanking the team for supporting people with oncological conditions. Partnership documentation covers hospital work across multiple countries and is presented with an explicit distinction between resources already delivered and offers of future collaboration.
good.realWorld_zh: 就一支高中團隊而言，同意與隱私的做法明確得不尋常：所有活動都事先透過書信、電話與前置探訪與接待機構協調；由家長或法定代理人給予許可，拍照另外單獨徵求同意，因此家長不同意的孩子不會被拍攝；參與者可以拒絕某項活動、某張照片或某個問題；原始照片與影片的取用權僅限於參訪團隊與接待機構的指定代表，而發布則須先取得該機構同意；團隊並表明，因此他們的照片並不代表所有參與者或所有活動。Girls Go First 的獎金也經過正式的同意相關文件程序。開放資源包括：公開資料夾中的四份三語刊物、課程錄影、依年齡分級的書籍、科學著色活動與填字遊戲、各式指南與工作坊方法，而完整方法則可透過夥伴關係在一個公開的聯絡地址取得。外部肯定包括吉爾吉斯共和國衛生部於 2026 年 4 月 22 日發出的一封信函，感謝團隊對腫瘤疾病患者的支持。夥伴關係文件涵蓋跨多國的醫院工作，並明確區分已經交付的資源與未來合作的意向。

gemsTakeaway: Copy two habits: publish your stakeholder questions before the interviews so you cannot retrofit your conclusions, and shift the planning question from 'what can we deliver during a visit?' to 'what will remain afterwards?' - which is what turned a hospital workshop into 12 take-home kits and turned 23 school visits into nine schools now running the activities themselves.
gemsTakeaway_zh: 照抄兩個習慣：在訪談之前就先公開你的利害關係人問題，這樣你就無法事後把結論回頭套上去；以及把規劃時要問的問題，從「我們在一次探訪中能交付什麼？」換成「探訪結束之後還會留下什麼？」而正是這個轉換，把一場醫院工作坊變成了 12 份可帶回家的套件，也把 23 場校園參訪變成現在有九所學校自己在辦這些活動。
